title: Defect/RCCA: cross-session double-claim - two sessions claimed the same backlog item (BI-PF-0396)
body:
## Observed
`wg work --epic BI-PF-0390` returned `assigned: true` for **BI-PF-0396** while ANOTHER session already held it
-> the same backlog item was claimed by two sessions (double-claim). A claim must fail closed if the item is taken.

## RCCA (5-Why)
1. BI-PF-0396 was assigned to two sessions at once.
2. The lease lives in the git-shared item file (`item.execution{}`) but the other session's claim was only in
   THEIR working copy (uncommitted/unpushed) -> invisible to my instance -> seen as free.
3. Each session runs its OWN PF API instance over a SEPARATE working copy -> two assignment authorities.
4. ADR-0003 assumes ONE PF (single assignment authority); N dev instances break it (the lease is only shared after
   a commit/push, which is racy).
5. No guard detects a second instance / foreign token / an uncoordinated (unpushed) lease.

ROOT CAUSE: multiple PF API instances == multiple assignment authorities; the per-item lease is not globally
coordinated at claim time (same class as BI-PF-0457, fixed for ids via a git-CAS authority).

## Corrective
Adopt a SINGLE shared PF API instance (one assignment authority) that all sessions use (shared URL + token);
optionally coordinate the lease through a shared git-remote CAS (like the id counter) for cross-instance/offline.

## Fixed where (planned)
core/job_manager.py (claim path), scripts/dev/dev_server.py (single-instance guard), docs/OPERATIONS.
Tracked by backlog BI-PF-1261.

## Guard (preventive)
Refuse/detect a second dev API on an owned port; a claim finding `execution.worker_id` set (even unpushed) fails
closed; verify the lease round-trips via the shared authority.

rcca.root_cause: multiple PF API instances = multiple assignment authorities; per-item lease not coordinated at claim time
rcca.corrective: ONE shared PF API instance (single assignment authority) all sessions use; optional git-CAS lease for cross-instance atomicity
